Choose the job

A buy button and a bank payout are different products

A customer buys USDC inside a wallet in seconds. Later, they try to withdraw to a bank and discover that the same provider does not support their currency, account type or sell direction. The integration worked, but the journey was only half built. Start the shortlist from the full route your customer needs, including the point at which they can actually use the proceeds.

An on-ramp is fiat to crypto. An off-ramp is crypto to fiat. An institution redeeming an issuer's stablecoin, a merchant accepting a crypto invoice and an app embedding a consumer checkout may all use these words while buying different services. Choose the operating model before comparing company names.

Six ways to move between crypto and fiat
ModelUseful forWhat to establish
Embedded rampWallet or app users buying or selling supported cryptoEnd-user eligibility, checkout/KYC owner, payment method and support handoff
Ramp aggregatorProducts comparing or routing among execution providersProvider selection, quote source, identity reuse, execution counterparty and fallback behavior
Business exchange or OTCA company converting its own treasury or trade proceedsBusiness-account access, execution, withdrawal rails and bank-account ownership
Institutional issuer redemptionEligible entities redeeming the issuer's supported assetAccount approval, token/network, redemption conditions and banking schedule
Stablecoin payout orchestrationPlatforms, suppliers, payroll and marketplace disbursementBeneficiary onboarding, local rails, funds-in-transit and reconciliation
Merchant acceptance or spendingReceiving customer payments or spending a balanceInvoice or card product, merchant settlement, disputes and refund allocation

Peer-to-peer marketplaces add counterparty, payment-reversal and dispute risks. A payment card may let someone spend a balance without depositing fiat into their bank. Neither should be treated as an interchangeable substitute for an approved business payout API. Evaluate these alternatives separately and avoid using a personal account for a company's customer funds.

For tokenized assets, add another step: the issuer, fund administrator or transfer agent may need to approve and execute redemption before a ramp receives a supported stablecoin. A provider's USDC sell flow does not prove that a security token, fund interest or property claim can be redeemed. See the tokenization platform directory for the separate issuance and lifecycle role.

Coverage that matters

Write one complete corridor before asking who is best

A country count is a discovery signal, not a route specification. Record the customer's residence and entity type, source currency and rail, buy or sell direction, asset and chain, receiving currency and method, and beneficiary account type. Add transaction size, frequency, business purpose and whether payment is first-party or third-party. Then ask candidates to confirm that exact combination.

A route specification for the buyer brief
FieldWhat to writeWhy it changes the answer
Customer and purposeIndividual, business, platform user, merchant or institutional distributorEligibility and onboarding differ by customer and product
DirectionBuy, sell, treasury conversion, merchant settlement or third-party payoutOn-ramp coverage does not establish sell or payout coverage
Money inCurrency, payment rail, originating account and account holderCards, bank transfers and local methods have different controls and finality
Onchain legToken, contract where relevant, network and source/destination walletThe same token ticker on another chain may not be accepted
Money outCurrency, receiving rail, beneficiary type and account holderLocal banking access and recipient checks are corridor-specific
Quote and fundingAmount, quote expiry, rate lock and funding deadlineLate or incorrect funding may change delivery or require a new instruction
Evidence of successProvider status, transaction hash, bank reference and recipient creditDifferent systems can report completion at different points
Failure and exitTimeout, return route, support owner and termination accessAn accepted deposit can still be followed by a failed conversion or bank payout

Compare supported configurations returned for the intended production account, not just marketing copy or sample API responses. Country lists, asset lists and payment-method lists may each be accurate without their intersection supporting your route. Feature enablement and account-specific restrictions still matter. Recheck before launch and after a provider or product change.

Regions also contain very different currencies and banking systems. An EU statement does not automatically cover the UK; a US availability statement may have state conditions; Asia-Pacific and Africa are not single payment corridors. Ask for the actual local method, entity and user eligibility instead of substituting a regional label.

Latin America

Brazil PIX and Mexico SPEI need separate route checks

Latin America is a collection of country-specific payment journeys. A company paying suppliers in Mexico is not necessarily buying the same product as a Brazilian individual funding a wallet. Start with the two countries and directions you need most, then expand only after the transaction and exception tests work.

Local-rail questions for Latin America
MarketRoute to specifyBuyer checks
Brazil / BRLPIX pay-in or PIX payout, explicitly separatedCustomer residence and entity type; CPF/CNPJ or required identity data; beneficiary key/account validation; eligible funding token and network
Mexico / MXNSPEI collection or payoutCLABE and beneficiary details; originating/receiving entity; account validation; tracking reference and receipt; return handling
Colombia / COPThe particular bank, ACH/PSE or instant-payment product offeredDistinguish collection from disbursement; recipient/account requirements; operating window and evidence of credit
Argentina / ARSThe specific local bank or account-based transfer routeEligible account type and holder; sender/recipient requirements; conversion assumptions; current operating terms
Cross-border flowSource fiat or stablecoin to destination local currencyWho performs FX, who holds funds, which local partner pays, and what happens if the bank leg fails

PIX support is directional

Banco Central do Brasil describes Pix as Brazil's instant account-to-account payment method. That describes the domestic rail, not a guarantee about a crypto provider's entire conversion journey. Funding confirmation, screening, conversion and recipient handling can add separate steps.

MoonPay's payment-method documentation reviewed on November 24 lists PIX for BRL purchases in Brazil. It does not establish a PIX payout merely because a buy method is listed. Its current notice also describes temporary restrictions on other BRL purchase methods. Confirm the live checkout rather than assuming the card and wallet methods shown elsewhere apply in Brazil.

Bridge documents separate rail enablement

Bridge's BRL guide describes PIX pay-ins, transfers and liquidation-address off-ramps, with sales access and rail endorsements. Its guide differentiates customer types and on-ramp/off-ramp access and points to changed endorsement requirements effective June 15, 2026. Use the current approval and migration process for the intended customer, not an old country-support screenshot.

The MXN guide describes SPEI virtual accounts, transfers and liquidation-address off-ramps with separate rail access. It also documents CLABE validation. These are documented product capabilities, not confirmation that your business or every beneficiary will be accepted. A virtual collection account and an external payout account can have different rules.

Compare institutional routes, not just widgets

Bitso Business's August 20, 2025 material describes stablecoin liquidity linked to PIX and SPEI, while Conduit's current product menu includes both rails in its business payment offering. These are starting points for a business proposal, not an independent test of their speed, authorization or availability. Request current customer eligibility and operating entities; do not reuse historical benchmark figures as a forecast.

For Mexico, Banco de Mexico's SPEI payment-information resource explains tracking and receipt evidence. Ask how the provider exposes the appropriate reference and how your support team can investigate a pending or returned payment. Do not publish customer account details or tracking data in public dashboards.

Conversion without confusion

KYC, KYB and bank ownership are different checks

Map partner KYB, end-user KYC, beneficiary validation and transaction screening separately. The business integrating an API may need approval before any production customer can use it. A verified person may still be ineligible for a particular product, amount, payment method or jurisdiction. A valid bank account may still be unsuitable for a third-party payout.

Allocate who collects information, verifies it, makes the decision, stores evidence, handles a manual review and communicates the result. If identity reuse is offered, establish the accepted provider, product, country and contract conditions. Do not assume an aggregator can carry one verification pass across every execution provider.

Keep the journey proportionate and clear

Explain required steps before the customer commits money. Distinguish a missing field, a technical failure, a review in progress and a final eligibility decision. Preserve progress where appropriate and provide a safe return path from hosted verification. Use clear field labels, ordinary website-address input where needed, mobile-friendly controls and actionable error messages without removing required checks.

Test consent and terms screens, document uploads, browser redirects, wallet handoffs and interrupted sessions. Make sure an accessibility or mobile-keyboard problem does not become a misleading compliance rejection. Compare completion by country and method using the same eligible cohort; do not attribute every abandoned checkout to KYC.

Fraud and liability need explicit owners

Ask who handles card disputes, stolen credentials, account takeover, suspicious wallets and sanctions alerts. For bank-funded journeys, establish account-name matching and whether third-party deposits are permitted. For payouts, ask about beneficiary changes and confirmation before irreversible movement. Screening software and a financial service counterparty have different responsibilities.

Review the exact contracting entity and the service permissions relevant to your activities with the responsible professionals. A registration, group brand or local banking partner does not automatically cover every part of the route. Platform and payment access are separate from a conclusion about your own legal obligations.

Quotes and settlement

Compare what arrives, when it arrives and why

Compare timestamped quotes for the same route and customer assumptions. For buying, record the fiat debited and crypto delivered. For selling, record the crypto sent and fiat actually credited. Use consistent token units, networks and quote timestamps. Otherwise a cheaper-looking rate can simply reflect a different funding method, stale market snapshot or excluded charge.

Review provider charges, payment processing, spread, FX conversion, network costs, payout deductions and intermediary-bank adjustments. Some are already included in a quoted amount; do not add them twice. A zero-fee label is not proof that all of those components disappear. Ask for the current commercial schedule privately rather than relying on an undated universal price table.

Estimate, locked quote and final receipt

An estimate can change before execution. A locked quote has conditions such as validity, funding deadline and qualifying amount. A completed receipt states what was actually delivered. Ask who bears currency movement between each step, and whether a refund returns the original asset amount, fiat value or a newly converted balance. Do not imply that moving into a stablecoin removes issuer, depeg, network or counterparty risk.

Do not compress these milestones into instant settlement
MilestoneEvidence to requestRemaining dependency
Instruction acceptedOrder ID, accepted route and quote detailsEligibility, funding and execution may still be pending
Fiat funding acceptedProvider receipt and payment referencePayment reversals or compliance review may still apply
Crypto confirmedTransaction hash, network and confirmation ruleConversion and bank payout can remain outstanding
Conversion completedExecuted amounts and rate recordBank submission and recipient credit remain separate
Payout submittedBank/provider reference and submission timestampReceiving institution may reject, delay or return it
Recipient creditedAppropriate status or receipt evidence with agreed meaningLater corrections or returns need their own handling

Report timing from agreed start and end events. Separate ordinary business-day processing, weekend handling, bank holidays, review cases and network congestion. Ask for measured percentile data and the excluded cases rather than interpreting a domestic instant rail or a fast demo as a universal end-to-end SLA.

For larger business flows, discuss liquidity, prefunding, available balance, daily capacity, transaction limits, treasury approvals and execution windows. Ask how a provider handles a concentration spike or banking-partner outage. A virtual IBAN is a routing identifier; inspect the actual account holder, institution, ledger, safeguarding or custody arrangement and withdrawal rights before treating it as a bank account in your own name.

Design for the difficult case

When crypto arrives but the payout does not

Payment integrations are often demonstrated on the happy path. Procurement should also establish who resolves the case in which the customer has sent value and cannot use the proceeds. Agree the supported return asset, chain and address, customer notifications, escalation owner and reconciliation treatment before launch.

Exception scenarios to test with the provider
ScenarioDecision to settleEvidence and handling
Expired quote or late fundingExecute, reprice, hold or return?Funding deadline, customer approval and new quote linkage
Underpayment or overpaymentComplete a partial order, request more, or return excess?Amount tolerance, support owner and ledger adjustment
Wrong token, chain or missing memoIs recovery possible and who may attempt it?Accepted deposit rules and documented recovery limitations
Beneficiary or account mismatchReject before sending, review or return?Validation result, safe correction process and audit trail
Crypto received, fiat bank leg rejectedWhere and when is value returned?Return currency/network/address, deductions and escalation
Duplicate or delayed webhookHow do you avoid double credit or payout?Signature validation, event identifiers, idempotency and status lookup
Chargeback after crypto deliveryWho bears the loss and investigates?Dispute agreement, evidence duties and reserve treatment
Provider outage or route suspensionCan another route be used safely?Original order state, refund/release decision and approved fallback

Webhooks are notifications, not the entire ledger

Validate webhook authenticity according to the selected product's documentation. Handle duplicate delivery and out-of-order updates where documented, and make processing idempotent. Preserve provider order IDs, your own references, chain transactions and bank references in the appropriate protected systems. Use authoritative status retrieval and reconciliation for unresolved states rather than treating a callback or checkout redirect as unconditional success.

Never share seed phrases or private keys with a support agent. Verify refund instructions through the agreed secure channel, especially if an address changes during an incident. Wrong-network transfers can be unrecoverable. Do not promise recovery merely because the interface offers a support form.

Aggregator fallback needs its own design

Do not retry with another provider until you know whether the first order accepted funds or created an irreversible instruction. A fresh checkout can trigger another identity journey, rate or payment attempt. Specify how the user sees the new execution provider and terms and how your systems prevent duplicate funding or credit.

Require a support responsibility map across your app, aggregator, execution provider, liquidity or banking partner and recipient institution. Give customers one clear contact path without pretending one company controls every downstream decision. Keep a case log linking the original order, exception, return and any replacement order.

Evidence before launch

A pilot plan for conversion, reliability and finance

Use sandbox and documented test modes first. They establish integration behavior, not actual bank acceptance, liquidity or production approval. Any controlled production test should be separately authorized by the business with appropriate controls; this research did not move funds or test authenticated payment APIs.

  1. Obtain written approval for the product, route and customer types.
  2. Confirm the supported asset/network and beneficiary configuration for that environment.
  3. Test onboarding, hosted redirects and return-to-app behavior on desktop and mobile.
  4. Check quote expiry, source and destination amounts, rate-lock conditions and fee presentation.
  5. Exercise the permitted success and failure scenarios, including interrupted sessions.
  6. Verify webhook authentication, duplicate handling and authoritative status recovery.
  7. Reconcile orders with the chain and bank evidence appropriate to the route.
  8. Confirm support ownership, escalation access and the customer communication plan.
  9. Agree production observation windows, exclusions, volume controls and a pause decision.
  10. Recheck assumptions after changes to product versions, accounts, rails or counterparties.

Use meaningful conversion denominators

Track sessions that are eligible for the selected route, checkout starts, identity steps, accepted payment instructions, completed conversion and confirmed payout outcomes separately. Segment by product, country, direction, method and device. Count spam and ineligible attempts transparently rather than using them selectively to make a provider look better or worse.

Report time to completion alongside review, return and failure rates. An authorized card payment is not crypto delivered; a provider's completed status may not have the meaning your finance team expects. Reconcile analytics with stored orders and financial records. Email notifications are an operational signal, not the system of record.

Finance and tax reporting

Agree statement and transaction-export access, identifiers, timestamps, gross/net amounts, rate records, adjustments and retention. Ask finance and the relevant tax professionals how conversions, disposals, issuer redemptions and payment services should be recorded for the actual business and jurisdictions. A provider-generated form or export does not automatically settle the customer's reporting obligations.

Minimize sensitive data in monitoring and avoid putting personal documents, account numbers or wallet-to-person mappings in analytics URLs. Allocate access, retention and deletion with the appropriate teams. Preserve operational evidence without creating an unnecessary public record of customer financial activity.

Build the shortlist

Send every provider the same corridor brief

Describe the current product, customer, country, direction, fiat rail, token and chain. Explain whether you are moving your company's funds, serving app users, settling merchants or paying third parties. State required time windows and operational constraints without sending confidential customer records in the first enquiry.

  1. Which product and contracting entity will serve this exact route?
  2. Which customer and beneficiary types are eligible, and which countries or subregions are excluded?
  3. Which pay-in and payout methods are enabled independently?
  4. Who collects, verifies, decides, stores and escalates KYC/KYB and transaction checks?
  5. Which tokens, chains, wallet models and network confirmations are accepted?
  6. Is the displayed amount an estimate, a locked quote or a completed receipt?
  7. Who holds fiat and crypto at every step, and what rights apply to those balances?
  8. What is the timing definition, and which review, bank or holiday cases are excluded?
  9. What happens after late funding, wrong-network deposits or rejected payouts?
  10. How do webhooks, status lookups, replay and idempotency behave?
  11. Which reports connect the order, chain transfer, bank reference and return?
  12. Who supports the customer and what happens during an outage or account suspension?
  13. What liquidity, prefunding, limits and approval controls apply at the proposed volume?
  14. How can the business export records, reconcile open orders and exit the service?

Compare evidence, exclusions and responsibilities rather than awarding the contract to the longest country list. A narrow route with a clear return path can be more useful than a large coverage claim whose buy and sell conditions are unclear. No directory ranking, integration badge or compliance label replaces your own technical, commercial and professional review.

Questions buyers ask

Fiat on-ramp and crypto off-ramp FAQs

What is a crypto on-ramp and off-ramp?

An on-ramp converts fiat into crypto; an off-ramp converts crypto into fiat delivered through an eligible payment method. A wallet transfer, exchange trade or stablecoin balance alone is not evidence that fiat reached a bank account.

Which fiat ramp provider is best?

The best fit depends on the customer type, country, direction, fiat currency, payment rail, asset, network and integration product. Compare one complete route at a time and test onboarding, net delivery, exceptions and support rather than choosing from country totals alone.

Which crypto off-ramp should a business use?

Compare an eligible business exchange account, institutional issuer redemption, a payment or OTC relationship, stablecoin orchestration, or an embedded end-user sell flow. These models have different account, KYB, custody and recipient requirements.

Can PIX on-ramp support be used as proof of PIX off-ramp support?

No. Receiving BRL to buy crypto and paying BRL to a beneficiary are different directions. Confirm the selected product, enabled rail, customer type, destination account and live transaction eligibility separately.

How should I compare Latin America ramps?

Compare Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and Argentina separately. Name the local rail and currency, sender and recipient type, account requirements, funding token and network, quote behavior, operating limits and return path. A regional brand or country flag does not establish all of those conditions.

Does a stablecoin transaction mean the bank payout is complete?

No. Blockchain confirmation, provider conversion, bank submission and recipient credit are separate milestones. Define what each status means and request bank reference or receipt evidence where available before reporting payout success.

Can KYC be reused across providers?

Only under the particular product, agreement and jurisdiction conditions. Confirm collection, verification, decision, retention, reliance and escalation responsibilities. An aggregator or a prior KYC pass does not automatically satisfy another execution provider.

What happens if crypto arrives but the fiat payout fails?

Agree the return asset, network, address, fees, timing and approval process before launch. Determine whether a return is automatic or manual, and reconcile the failed payout and any replacement instruction to the original order. Do not assume an irreversible crypto transfer can be recalled.

How do I compare costs without a headline fee table?

Compare timestamped quotes for the same customer, direction, amount, asset/network and payment method. Review provider, processing, spread, FX, network and payout deductions, rate-lock terms and the net amount delivered. Avoid double-counting fees already included in the quote.

Does a virtual IBAN prove that funds are held in my own bank account?

No. Ask for the account holder, institution, ledger arrangement, safeguarding or custody terms, beneficial claim and withdrawal rights. A dedicated payment identifier does not by itself establish a separate deposit account or legal protection.

What is the difference between an aggregator and a direct ramp?

A direct ramp executes a defined service under its operating arrangement. An aggregator routes among underlying providers. Confirm which provider quotes and executes each order, how identity and support handoffs work, and how retries avoid duplicate payments.

Can a ramp guarantee tokenized-asset redemption?

No. A ramp converts or moves supported assets; it does not by itself redeem a fund interest, security token or property claim. Separate issuer or administrator redemption, investor restrictions, stablecoin conversion and the final bank payout.

Research and maintenance

How this guide uses evidence

FluidRWA Research Team reviewed current Google results for crypto off-ramp providers, additional Latin America comparisons and selected official product documentation on November 24, 2026. The guide separates documented scope from customer eligibility and operational performance. It is a buyer research resource, not a universal ranking or project-specific legal, financial or tax advice.

Selected current checks cover MoonPay, Transak, Banxa, Ramp Network, Stripe Onramp, Bridge, Circle Mint, Onramper, Conduit, Mesh, Sardine and Bitso Business material. Source publication dates and product limits are retained in the research record. No production funds were moved and no authenticated payment API was tested. The editorial update does not establish fresh verification of every historical directory entry or change the dates in the separate Network Explorer dataset.

The directory preserves its prior records and adds Bitso Business for institutional Latin America discovery. Legacy references and adjacent infrastructure are not presented as interchangeable end-to-end ramps. Use stablecoin payment infrastructure, KYC and AML providers and custody providers for adjacent roles. Inclusion alone does not confer a Vetted badge or establish authorization for your route.
